messages:
sara: noticed a 2.5x p95 increase on prod after the v1.12.3 rollout, starting ~09:17 UTC. graph here: https://internal.redwood/graphs/latency-spike :rotating_light:

mike: saw CI perf alerts too, several perf tests crossed threshold in the merge pipeline: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/4578 :eyes:

perf-bot: [perf-ci] test/smallseq_throughput: baseline=28k tok/s, current=11k tok/s, delta=-60% (threshold -20%)

oliver: started a quick bisect on the release branch. suspecting the kernel selector change from PR#4021 that altered small-seq pathing.

jun: profiler trace attached — allocation + L2 stall increased. looks like requests are routing to the fallback GEMM kernel when sequence length <= 32; previously we used the fused-attn microkernels.

lisa: that matches an experiment in the kernel selector to prefer generic kernels for padded batches. was the padding policy changed in that PR? @oliver

oliver: yes, PR#4021 changed the heuristics: if average_seq_len < 20 && padding_ratio > 0.4 => pick generic path. I can reproduce locally with our smallseq benchmark.

priya: can you paste the local repro command? we need an emergency rollback plan if this blocks more rollouts.

oliver: repro cmd:
```
./bench --model gpt-j --seq-len 16 --batch 8 --padding 0.5 --kernels=auto
```
local p95 before: 8.2ms, after: 21.1ms.

mike: file a revert PR for the selector change and include the test case that triggered it. also mark the rollout blocker. I'll pause canary expansion. @deploy-bot please hold canary.

deploy-bot: Canary expansion paused for v1.12.3 as requested by mike.

oliver: opening revert PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4099 (quick revert of selector tweak). request review from @lisa @jun.

perf-bot: running CI on PR#4099...

perf-bot: [ci] all perf tests passed on PR#4099, smallseq_throughput restored to baseline (diff +2%).

mike: great — proceeding to rollback the change in prod. Sara, want to resume canary after rollback verification?

sara: yes, once rollback live metrics show p95 back to baseline for 30 minutes. I’ll monitor.

jun: postmortem notes: root cause = kernel selector change reacted poorly to padded micro-batches — bumped into a path where fused kernels were avoided. the selector used padding_ratio threshold that wasn't validated across seq distribution.

lisa: action items proposal:
- add microbench variants for seq lengths [8,16,32,64] with mixed padding
- add explicit KV cache eviction / hit-rate test to perf-suite
- tighten perf test thresholds for smallseq_throughput and use median-of-5 samples instead of single run to reduce flakiness

priya: will add the microbench and KV tests to the perf harness. also propose gating PR merges on smallseq_throughput not regressing > 10% in CI.

oliver: I'll update the kernel selector logic to include a fallback check: only switch to generic if perf-sim says win > 5% across 3 sample distributions. and add unit tests for the heuristic.

perf-bot: noted flaky test: test/kv_cache_eviction was showing 20% variance; switching to median-of-7 reduced false positives in experiments.

lisa: also found a nondeterministic seed in the microbench runner that caused noise. fix in #4102 will pin RNG and increase samples.

sara: OK team — thanks for quick turnaround. please post PR links for the test hardening work when available. I'll schedule a 30-min retro tomorrow to review threshold values and add to the oncall playbook.

mike: +1. assign owners: oliver (selector fix), priya (new microbench + gating), lisa (flaky test fix), jun (profiler checklist). target EOD Fri for PRs. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: summary: rollback deployed, metrics trending to baseline, action items created.

sara: closing thread for now, reopening if we see any regression during canary resume.
